source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 3:11 (Masorah triple with 2 Kgs 6:27)
claim_en: ha-min ('is it from...?') occurs exactly twice in the TORAH: Gen 3:11 (the tree question to Adam) and Num 20:10 (the rock question at Meribah) - the Kitzur: as death was decreed through the one, death was decreed through the other

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 3:11 (sofei tevot, final letters)
claim_en: The final letters of asher tzivitikha le-vilti akhol ('which I commanded you not to eat') spell rakhil ('talebearer') - 'for you went after the talebearer's counsel'

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 3:6 (Masorah, four in Scripture)
claim_en: la-enayim ('to the eyes' - the tree as a delight to the eyes) is Torah-unique to Gen 3:6; the Masorah's other three tokens are in the Prophets and Writings

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:10 ('naked-I, naked-you: both defective')
claim_en: erom ('naked', singular) occurs exactly twice in the Torah - the man's confession 'naked am I' (3:10) and God's echo 'who told you that naked are you' (3:11), both inside this span
Both erom tokens are written DEFECTIVE (no vav) - zero full spellings

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:7 (the Hilleli-codex full/defective dispute recorded)
claim_en: erumim ('naked', plural, after the eating) is written doubly defective in SNAPSHOT - no vav and no final yod - against the FULL arumim of 2:25 before the sin: the naked-word's spelling strips as the couple falls

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:5 ('ki yodea: defective vav... and so every Torah knowledge-form of its class')
claim_en: yodea ('knows' - 'for God knows') at 3:5 is written DEFECTIVE, no vav

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:5 ('yodee: defective as above')
claim_en: yode ('knowers of good and evil' - the serpent's promise) at 3:5 is written DEFECTIVE, no vav

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:9 ('ayeka: dagesh in the yod')
claim_en: aye-ka ('Where are you?' - the first divine question) carries a dagesh (doubling dot) in its yod

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:7 (the leaf-spelling Masorah note)
claim_en: The leaf-noun aleh has exactly THREE Torah tokens: the fig leaf of the fall (3:7), the olive leaf in the dove's mouth at the flood's end (8:11), and the driven leaf whose sound chases the exiled (Lev 26:36) - shame, hope, terror

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 3:1 (a revia pause-accent on the quoted phrase, per the cited authority)
claim_en: A revia (pause accent) marks amar Elohim lo tokhelu ('God said: you shall not eat') in the tradition Minchat Shai cites; SNAPSHOT's accent chain there reads differently

check.note: manuscript-variant gap - SNAPSHOT shows munach/zaqef qatan on the phrase; the revia is another tradition's reading
